extracted.intended_audience: authors and editors of Cochrane systematic reviews (reviews of interventions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors and editors preparing and maintaining Cochrane systematic reviews of interventions, covering planning, searching, data collection, bias assessment, analysis, GRADE, interpretation, and related methodological expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Handbook / standard methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The Handbook describes in detail the process of preparing and maintaining Cochrane systematic reviews on the effects of healthcare interventions and includes guidance on the standard methods applicable to every review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics listed as standard methods: planning a review, searching and selecting studies, data collection, risk of bias assessment, statistical analysis, GRADE and interpreting results; also covers specialised topics (non-randomized studies, adverse effects, complex interventions, equity, economics, patient-reported outcomes, individual patient data, prospective meta-analysis, and qualitative research).

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning a review
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on planning a review is one of the standard methods applicable to every Cochrane review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning is treated as a core methodological element authors should consult the Handbook for; no further detail on this page (see relevant Handbook chapter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching and selecting studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on searching and selecting studies is a standard method applicable to every Cochrane review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should follow Handbook guidance on literature searching and selection procedures (see relevant chapter for detailed standards and examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on data collection from included studies is a standard method applicable to every Cochrane review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Handbook chapters for recommended data extraction processes, forms, and quality checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk of bias assessment is listed as a core standard method for Cochrane reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Handbook methods for assessing risk of bias (e.g., domain-based tools); see the corresponding chapter for instrument choice and application guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical analysis is identified among the standard methods applicable to every Cochrane review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handbook provides guidance on meta-analysis models, heterogeneity assessment, and sensitivity analyses; consult the statistical chapters for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRADE and interpreting results
rubrics_metrics.description: GRADE and interpreting results are included as standard elements of Cochrane reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook gives guidance on applying GRADE to assess certainty of evidence and on interpreting findings for decision-making; see GRADE-related chapters for criteria and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological Expectations for Cochrane Intervention Reviews (MECIR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key aspects of Handbook guidance are collated as the Methodological Expectations for Cochrane Intervention Reviews (MECIR), which provide core standards generally expected of Cochrane reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each MECIR item includes a link to a relevant Handbook chapter; MECIR items summarize core standards reviewers are expected to meet (see MECIR for itemised requirements and compliance expectations).

rubrics_metrics.name: How to cite the Handbook (online)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended citation for the full Handbook online: 'Higgins JPT, Thomas J, Chandler J, Cumpston M, Li T, Page MJ, et al, editor(s). Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5 (updated August 2024). Cochrane, 2024. Available from www.cochrane.org/handbook.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details of how to cite individual chapters are available in each chapter; a separate recommended format is provided for the print edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to cite the Handbook (print edition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended citation for the print edition: 'Higgins JPT, Thomas J, Chandler J, Cumpston M, Li T, Page MJ, et al, editor(s). Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions. 2nd Edition. Chichester (UK): John Wiley & Sons, 2019.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use chapter-specific guidance for citing individual chapters when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to re-use Handbook material — short quotations / academic non-commercial use
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic or other non-commercial re-use: you do not need to request permission to use short quotations (though these must be appropriately cited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If intending to reproduce material using screenshots, including exact figures or tables from the Handbook or including lengthy direct quotations (more than 5 lines of text), you must fill in a form to request permission; requests are sent to the Cochrane Support team and, if approved, are granted free of charge on condition the source is acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to re-use Handbook material — commercial use
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial re-use includes any use of the Handbook that will be used in a product for which there is a monetary fee, and/or where it is associated in any way with any product or service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For commercial re-use enquiries contact Wiley Global Permissions, John Wiley & Sons, Ltd.; separate permission process applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versions and changes / archived editions
rubrics_metrics.description: Archived copies of previous versions of the Handbook are available (versions 6.4, 6.3, 6.2, etc.; version 5.1: March 2011; earlier versions listed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details on how the Handbook has changed compared to previous versions and information on the update process are available on the Versions and changes page; note that version 5.2 reprinted only chapters 1, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 21 while others remain 5.1.0.
